_comment: THE AGENTIC HARNESS layer. Owner, 2026-09-20: "cat-harness, folio-assistant-core, folio-assistant are distinct instances/schemas" — so this declares itself `cat-harness` rather than `folio-assistant`. It carried the latter until the repository root gained a harness.json of its own, at which point TWO instances declared one name and `instanceRoots` — keyed on the declared name — could only hold one of them. The one it held was the root, so `folio-assistant` resolved to the checkout and the harness layer became unreachable by name. `stub` is UNCHANGED and stays `folio-assistant`: the stub names the PUBLISHED artefact (docs/folio-assistant/, _kg/folio-assistant.jsonld, the Pages path) and the name names the instance, which is the entire reason a declaration carries both. The CatHarness declaration for THIS instance — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.
_title: No `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the instance's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity.
name: cat-harness
_title_comment: The HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. Owner, 2026-09-21: "harnesses should list the names (they should be named in schmeas, e.g. cat-boostrap should be named 'Boostrap', f-a => Folio Assistant, cat-harness => C@T Harness)". `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against. Bean t3n8. THIS ONE WAS WRONG RATHER THAN ABSENT: it declared `title: "folio-assistant"`, the ROOT instance's name, so two instances carried one title and `disambiguate()` correctly qualified this tab to "folio-assistant (cat-harness)" — the label the owner reported. The disambiguator behaved as designed; the declaration was the defect.

images._avatarRegion_comment: RE-MEASURED on the owner's report, 2026-09-20: "last one too high". The first box was x 0.19 y 0.505 w 0.24 and it CLIPPED THE TOP OF THE HARD HAT — the hat's crown starts at y~0.51, so a box opening at 0.505 sat on it with nothing above. assets.title: AGENTS.md — cat-harness
assets.description: The cold-start file for an agent working IN this layer, and it is THIS LAYER'S own as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). It was declared `scope: "repository"`, so it resolved to the repository root's AGENTS.md — one file answering both "what binds everywhere" and "what binds in the harness layer", which is the conflation `readmeFinding` calls MAJOR for a non-root instance and could not report, because the asset DID resolve. It resolved to the wrong file's job. No `source`: this file is authored here. The root's carries the bootstrap provenance, because the root's is the file bootstrap copies at initialisation.

assets.title: cat-harness
assets.description: What this LAYER is, for a reader — as distinct from what the repository is, which is the root's README. Split from it on 2026-09-20 (issue #592); before that this instance had no README of its own and claimed the repository's. It does not list this instance's directories: `harness.json` is that list, and a second copy in prose is free to disagree with it the day a directory moves.

assets.title: Initializing into folio-assistant
assets.description: What bootstrap's step 2 reads once it has been pointed at THIS instance. Published at the fixed convention every cat-harness instance honours, composed by `initializationDoc()` rather than spelled, so bootstrap needs no per-target knowledge and can initialise into a SPECIALISED harness it was never written against. Declared as an asset as well as conventional, so `check:declared-assets` verifies it is there and that its links resolve: a convention nothing checks is a convention that is honoured until it quietly is not. The path is INSTANCE-relative here, not `<stub>/docs/...`: this instance has its own directory (`cat-harness/`), so `siteDir` is plain `docs`, and the stub names published artefacts rather than a directory. Whether bootstrap can still find it from one reference is open — see bean `wggr`.

_stub_comment: RENAMED from `folio-assistant` on 2026-09-21, on the owner's ruling, closing the collision issue #649 raised and bean `x3bd` flagged as settle-before-you-move. `artefactStub(d) = d.stub ?? d.name`, so this field is the ONLY stub declared anywhere in the tree — every other instance falls through to its `name`. While it read `folio-assistant` it was the string the REPOSITORY ROOT instance also carries as its `name`, so both resolved to `<base>/folio-assistant.jsonld`: two vocabularies, one path, and a reader dereferencing it got whichever layer answered. It is kept as an explicit field rather than deleted so the rename is visible where the collision was, and because `x3bd` records that this string names published artefacts (`.jsonld`, `.schema.json`, the viewer directory) rather than being cosmetic.
_publication_comment: The `publication host` axis of docs/proposals/deployment-topologies.md, accepted 2026-09-19 (issue #363). WHAT KIND of host serves the renderings — distinct from `canonicalUrl` (the base @ids are minted against) and from `readme.linkStyle` in harness.config.json (how a link to a published artefact is written). This instance really does publish to GitHub Pages, so it declares so; an instance that has not said is `undefined`, which is a third state and must never be read as `github-pages`.

stickies._comment: ONE CARD FOR THIS HARNESS, per the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20: "not all stickies should be cat harness they should be outputs (as if) each init harness ran ... each own intiaization sticky note to show sucess". It replaces three — `landing`, `cat-harness` and `subgraphs`. The first two are merged here because they were always this one harness talking about itself twice; the third moved to folio-assist-core, whose subject content IS.  `bodyFrom: description` rather than a literal body, so the c@t-harness derivation chain is read from the declaration above and cannot drift from it — the owner: "dont lose acronym definitions". `bodyAppend` carries the cat's introduction and the scope line, which is why that field exists.  THEME `grumpy-cat`, the sage hoodie, per "cat-harness=gumpy hoddie".

**Scope:** the platform — skills, schemas, processes, the MCP server and the pipeline. Not what a folio IS (that is folio-assist-core), and not any folio's own content, which lives in its own repository.

_folioMount_comment: R30, bean j2if. The library VIEW is a page a reader browses, so it carries the folio the same way a who-iris replica does — board-windows: "the test is not 'is this folio good' but 'is this the same folio'". These are the generated viewer pages whose rows offer a pull-out; check:folio-mount fails the build for one that lost the mount. Written as docs/cat-harness/library/ rather than a pattern because that is where viewerPlacement actually puts them, and a declaration that guessed would be a second copy of the mount table.

directories._coverage_comment: `docs` pointed at `cat-harness/docs/skills.md` until 2026-09-22 — a page titled "Skills & roles" whose headings are Skills, Roles and Capabilities, with no tools section in it. The tools graph had no documentation of its own and named a page about something else. That is worse than an absent ref, because an absent one is a legible gap while a ref that RESOLVES reports coverage: the check in force asks only whether the path exists, it did, and nothing ever flagged it. Found by applying the owner's instruction of 2026-09-21, "keep tools and skills separate!". `tool-graph.md` is the prose; `tools/index.md` is the generated view, and the two are different objects rather than two names for one.
directories.description: Tool definitions, one subdirectory per contributing instance (tools/<stub>/) so a composed instance adds its own without colliding on a filename. tools/index.ts merges them and is the only path a consumer imports. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The specifications this instance depends on, one record per specification, each pinning the EDITION in use and carrying the operative terms DERIVED from the corpus rather than hand-listed. Owner, 2026-09-20: "dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used" and "some schema that is operational should be in KG". UNDECLARED UNTIL 2026-09-22, which is the dh4f shape inverted: dh4f is a declared directory nothing holds, reported as a clean scan; this was a held directory nothing declared, so every consumer that fans out over declared directories skipped a registry that pins four external namespaces. It was reachable only by the one script that hardcodes its path. `dependents: reproduce` because a dependent folio consumes its own specifications — it inherits the convention, an id and a relative path, not this instance's records.

coverage._visualiser_comment: Declared 2026-09-23 under bean `yunp`: `external-schema` was one of the kinds with no published viewer, so the navbar listed it disabled and four records — an authority, an edition, its namespace IRIs, its dependents and its operative terms each — were reachable only by opening the JSON. ADDED TO THE COVERAGE BLOCK THAT WAS ALREADY HERE, not beside it: the first attempt wrote a second `coverage` key into the same object, which JSON permits and every parser resolves by taking the last — so the visualiser was silently discarded and the generator reported `no visualiser declared`. A duplicate key is not a merge.

directories.description: The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

UML class diagrams of every named sub-graph a harness declares — uml/overview/<instance>.puml|.mmd and uml/overview/<instance>/<sub-graph>.puml|.mmd — written from one model by scripts/gen-uml-overview.ts. The groupings are the declaration entries themselves and the classes are read from each graph kind's registered validator, so nothing here is authored. The rendered pages are docs/uml/overview/, which show the PlantUML rendering (docs/assets/img/uml/overview/, stamped with its source's hash) with the Mermaid beneath it, and link both sources. Owner, 2026-09-23.

The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Note the id is `kg` while the path is `skills/` — ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not. The `skills` graph does NOT owe a visualiser: `owesVisualiser` is `!renderable && holds !== "content"`, and `skills` is `content` — *"a graph that stands on its own does not need a viewer to be legible"*. So no gate was failing. What WAS wrong is that the viewer already existed and nothing declared it: `docs-auto` renders one sub-page per skills directory, and `graph-tiles.undeclaredProjections` lists exactly a directory with a published page and no declared visualisation — so all seven read as "no published viewer" in the navbar tiles while being rendered the whole time. `tools` is the same `content` kind and has declared one all along, which is the precedent: declaring a visualiser for a content kind is a courtesy the corpus already extends, not an obligation this invents.

Scenarios — the Roles an Actor takes on, in `roles.json`. A Role IS a BPMN swimlane: it carries the Skills its lane's activities need, the lanes it binds, and the Actor kinds that may play it. SPLIT OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21 so that "give me the Scenarios" is a query on the kind rather than a match on a path. One third of what this kind is named for is NOT here yet: a Role's `useCases` are free-text strings, so a User Story cannot be pointed at or traced to the Workflow it justifies.

Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from. The diagrams are the source of truth, not illustrations of one: a lane binds a Role, an activity names the Skill to run through `<folio:skill ref>`, and `workflow_complete` refuses a step that is not enabled. WHERE A RUNNING INSTANCE GOT TO is not here — that is `beans/workflows/`, kind `workflow-state`, which is `state` rather than `content`. Two questions, two graphs.

coverage._visualiser_comment: THE LIST FORM, so the entry can carry a title. Declared 2026-09-23 under bean `yunp`: `methodology` was one of seven kinds with no published viewer, which the build reports as a finding in `_data/harness.json` and the navbar renders as a disabled row. The page spans EVERY declared methodology graph, not this directory alone — `smart-kg/methodologies/` and `smart-base/methodologies/` are the same kind and their nodes are on it, labelled by declaring instance. directories.description: Judgement methodologies the harness owns, one sub-graph each: Kepner-Tregoe for a decision, MADR for its record, DMN for the computable case. PARALLEL rather than composable — which applies is contextual, and blending them produces a house method that cites nobody. Its own graph kind rather than skills, for three properties a skill does not have: extractable (somebody else's work, adopted, so it lifts out with its declaration when the field moves on), referenced rather than inlined (two skills quoting one method is two copies free to drift), and exempt from skill criteria (skill-is-brief caps an INSTRUCTION near 280 lines; a methodology is a faithful rendering of an external standard, and truncating it to fit a house limit would misrepresent the standard). GRADE is deliberately NOT here — see smart-kg-methodologies. RELOCATION, 2026-09-22, and the THREE declarations it removed. The owner: "dont bury sub-graph assets. same for <stub>/skills, etc." CRDM's three skills moved to `skills/crdm/`, RACI's to `skills/raci/`, and CRDM's eight diagrams to `processes/` — the stub-level graphs that were already declared. `methodology-crdm`, `methodology-raci` and `methodology-crdm-processes` are GONE rather than repointed: a separate entry for a directory that is already a package subdirectory of the declared `skills/` graph would declare one directory twice, which is the `x4v4` graph-inside-a-graph shape one level down. `gen-skill-docs` demonstrated it rather than anyone reasoning it out — it demanded a category under BOTH the basename and the declaration id, because both discovery branches found the same directory. So this entry now has the `methodology` graph to itself, holding exactly the four nodes and no subgraph: dmn, kepner-tregoe, madr, swot. This REVERSES the placement half of bean `g43o`; its argument that a reader should meet CRDM as a thing rather than as three prefixed filenames is preserved by the package manifest, which is what makes a skill package a thing everywhere else in this tree.

Everything a QA process produced, in one declared tree. The owner's rule, 2026-09-19: an artefact generated primarily as a QA reviewer belongs under `test/results/` as part of a QA process — placement follows PROVENANCE, not file family and not who fetches it afterwards. Three kinds live here and the FILES say which they are, per the `$schema` contract: `qa-results/v1` (`<producer>.qa-results.json`, a whole-artefact review — findings about a document the build just produced), `qa-witness/v1` (`witnesses/**`, one per audited subject in the families `block`, `kg` and `translation`, the published projection) and `kg-qa/v1` (`kg-qa/**`, the KG verdicts themselves — what `kg-audit` wrote). The `kg-qa/` tree MIRRORS each subject's path rather than being flat, and that is not tidiness: measured 2026-09-19, four sidecar basenames already occur twice across packages (`editor`, `getting-started`, `idle-backlog`, `l2-dak-authoring`), so a flat directory would silently overwrite four verdicts. `kgQaSidecarPath` in `schemas/kg-qa.ts` is the one answer for writer and reader alike. A directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and may hold more than one part of a graph; extension is a coincidence, a declaration inside the file is the contract. ONE entry rather than a nested set, deliberately: #263's own comment names the defect a declaration inside another declaration creates. STILL OUTSIDE: the 122 block verdicts `*.qa.json`, which sit beside their blocks and move next. The witnesses are PUBLISHED at `/assets/qa/`, which is where every badge points; the publishing workflows copy them into `_site/assets/qa/` after Jekyll, since Jekyll builds only `docs/`. Where a file lives and where it is served from are different questions.

directories._coverage_comment: THE OWNER RULED, 2026-09-21: render it, keep it off the canonical deploy. They asked to see this graph ("i eant to see beans/ todos/ fsh-guts/") and the description below says it is DELIBERATELY unrendered so something can be kept without being published. Both were wanted, so `publish: "staging-only"` is the third answer: `compose-docs.ts` withholds the page unless told `--staging`, which a local build and a STAGING preview pass and the canonical deploy does not. The default is the restrictive one because the two failure directions are not symmetric -- a forgotten flag loses a page from a preview, where whoever is looking at the preview sees it missing, while the opposite default publishes withheld content with nothing to show for it. The page INDEXES rather than republishes: each entry links to the file, so the graph stays the one copy.
directories.description: The trashcan that is kept. Deprecated and throwaway structured content — addressable, exported as <base>/fsh-guts.jsonld, and DELIBERATELY absent from the rendered site. Every other declared kind here is non-renderable because it is a graph a tool reads and there was never a page to make of it; this one's contents could be rendered and are not, so that something can be kept without being published. It is also the destination that makes the never-delete rule enforceable beyond beans: AGENTS.md forbids deleting a bean because a scrapped item stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one cannot be told from an accident, and that reasoning was always general — an agent removing a page or a script had only `rm`. Delete now means relocate here, and relocate is reversible. Files declare themselves with `$schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1`, per the same contract the bean and workflow stores use. NOTE on the name: `.fsh` is FHIR Shorthand in this codebase and across the WHO SMART folios; the collision was raised and the owner confirmed this spelling. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

Repository health reports — what the daily sweep under `test/health/` wrote. One `health-report/v1` document, declaring itself with a `$schema` tag rather than being duck-typed by path: a directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and the files inside say what they are. A SEPARATE graph from `qa`, and the line between them is about the SUBJECT, not the producer: a QA verdict judges an artefact this repository produced, against criteria that artefact is supposed to meet; a health report judges the REPOSITORY ITSELF — how big it has grown, how much of the publish branch the review previews occupy, whether the work plan has duplicates in it. Folding it into `qa` would leave a consumer asking for verdicts about this instance's content holding a fact about its clone. NOTE the path: it was `tests/health/results/` when this graph landed in #395, because this repository then had BOTH `test/` (the `qa` graph) and `tests/` (the Playwright e2e specs), and the owner asked for `tests/health`. #395 flagged that inconsistency in `skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md` rather than resolving it, since relocating a declared directory as a side effect of adding a check is the `dh4f` shape, where a consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. The owner settled it on `test/` the same day and it moved as its own change — bean `auap`, PR #400. The `id` here is unchanged, deliberately: an inheriting instance overrides on the entry's id and never on its path, so `health` still binds after the relocation. The e2e specs came to the declaration rather than the declaration to the specs, because `testDir` is one line of one config file and a declared path is what every downstream override resolves against.

Bean `frs5` moved all four entries out (the three IRIS items to who-iris, milnorlink to folio-assistant-sci) because the platform holds no content, and this entry was removed with them. Remove this and every downstream folio silently stops getting a library. IT IS THE `dh4f` SHAPE AND THAT IS KNOWN, NOT OVERLOOKED: a declared directory this instance does not hold is exactly what that bean is about. The cost is paid deliberately and it is bounded — the consumers that scan libraries now fan out over EVERY declared one (bean `a02m`), so an empty one contributes nothing rather than shadowing the two that have content. The real fix is the core relocation — `uploads`, `voices`, `translation-sources` and this moving to folio-assistant-core, per the owner's earlier "voices, uploads library in folio-asst-core" — after which a dependent inherits them from the layer that owns content and this entry goes for good.

Declared beside `smart-kg-methodologies` and for the same reason it is separate from it: `smart-kg` holds judgement methodologies for L1 guideline development (GRADE), and DIIG is a programme-investment method, which is a different job. `methodology-adoption` SS4 places a method by ownership so that extraction is literal -- this directory lifts out with this entry and nothing else moves. Issue #877, bean `wkt1`.

Declared SEPARATELY from `smart-base-methodologies` for the reason `methodology-crdm-processes` is declared separately from `methodologies/`: `workflowDirs` resolves diagrams from a declared directory, so a nested one that is not itself declared leaves every diagram undiscovered (bean `g43o`). Issue #877, bean `qnvy`.

Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph itself -- 241 markdown files, the entire published surface, and UNDECLARED until 2026-09-20. That is the dh4f defect in its purest form: every declaration-driven consumer scanned straight past the thing readers actually see. Owner, same day: 'docs/ is about documentation about the KG itself... docs/ in cat-harness', with the intent that this is WHERE DOCUMENTATION GOES and therefore the only place a forward reference may be authored. The `docs` kind is RENDERABLE and is registered by `schemas/docs-graph-kind.ts` rather than added to BASE_GRAPH_KINDS, so the assertion that the harness's base vocabulary carries no renderable kind stays true and its test stays unchanged. Distinct from `folio`, which is core's: the difference is the SUBJECT. A page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`; a note an author writes about an ingested catalogue is a `folio`; the catalogue itself is `library/`. `dependents` is `skip`, unlike the other renderable graph `folio`: this is documentation THIS instance publishes about the knowledge graph, so a dependent folio inherits the pages rather than an empty directory to refill — it authors its own subject matter under `folio/`, which is `reproduce`. CHANGED TO `reproduce` 2026-09-21 ON THE OWNER'S COMPOSE RULING (bean `n0nf`, issue #638), and the paragraph above is kept rather than deleted because its reasoning was right for the question it answered. It argued `skip` on the grounds that a dependent should INHERIT THE PAGES rather than get an empty directory to refill. Under compose it gets BOTH: the pages still reach it, and `reproduce` gives it the place to override one. So this is not a reversal of that argument, it is the second half of it arriving. The `dependents` doc warns that defaulting to `reproduce` ships junk -- twelve inherited directories, four of them the platform's own, each empty with a committed keep marker, the `dh4f` shape shipped downstream. That warning is about a DEFAULT, and the test it turns on is the one that schema states: is this directory part of the SHAPE a folio has, or merely where THIS instance's content lives? Before the ruling `docs/` was the second. After it, a folio is expected to author and override its own documentation, which makes it the first -- the same answer `uploads/` and `library/` get, and they are `reproduce` and also start empty. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO is give the REPOSITORY ROOT a `docs/`. The root does not depend on cat-harness (measured: its declaration chain has length 1), so nothing is inherited there, and the root's own `harness.json` carries the owner's "only uploads/ on this repo's root". `n0nf` says the root's docs "is not its own: cat-harness installs it", which needs a dependency edge that does not exist. That is left for the owner rather than settled here. A viewer IS declared for this `docs` directory, and `owesVisualiser` not demanding one is not the same as forbidding one. The kind is `renderable`, so it does not OWE a viewer — but the owner's rule, quoted in full in `mount-instance-docs.ts`'s module note, is that a harness which instantiates a directory MAKES a visualiser for it, docs and library included. It points at the `docs-auto` index, NOT at the mount route `/docs/<instance>/`: that mount is a VERBATIM copy of the directory, and `visualiserHref` exists precisely because linking a rail to it lands on a byte-identical page — the owner's *"clicking on doc/ ... under who-iris navbar did nothing"*. The owner's sentence is CITED rather than quoted here on purpose: it names a graph whose viewer is `publish: "staging-only"`, and a test asserts that name appears NOWHERE in the built export — including in a declaration's own prose, which is where quoting it put it. The test caught that, and this paragraph is the second attempt.

THE REPOSITORY ROOT'S DOCUMENTATION OVERLAY, managed by this instance. Owner's ruling, 2026-09-21, answering whether the root declares its own docs: "harness can have docs/ which then get listed under cat-harness/docs/<harness>, there is also docs/ dir in repo root managed by cat-harness. other harness augment or overlay ontop of that (content and behviors)". SEPARATE FROM THE `docs` ENTRY ABOVE, AND IT HAS TO BE. That one is instance-scoped and `reproduce`, which is what makes a DEPENDENT materialise its own docs/ (bean n0nf slice 1). This one is `scope: "repository"`, and a repository-scoped entry is filtered out for dependencies -- cat-harness.ts:3261 and :3507 both skip it unless `link.own`. Re-scoping the existing entry instead of adding this one would therefore have UNDONE slice 1 silently: a dependent would simply stop getting a docs/ and nothing would fail. Two directories answering two questions, so two entries, with distinct ids -- the convention `who-iris-docs` already follows. `dependents` is `skip` for the same reason every other cross-instance repository-scoped entry here is: a dependent never reaches this one at all, and claiming it reproduces would be a promise the resolver does not keep. WHAT MAKES IT NOT `dh4f`: a declared directory that nothing reads is this repository's most-paid-for defect, and an empty overlay is exactly that shape. It is consumed by the site build, which composes it OVER cat-harness/docs/ -- so what it contributes today is nothing VERIFIABLY, pinned by a test asserting an empty overlay produces a byte-identical site, rather than nothing unnoticed.

The CONTENT layer's schema nodes, staged as a top-level directory ahead of the split (#223). Owner, 2026-09-20: 'not in cat-harness, in folio-assitant-core/ as a named subgraph.' A NAMED SUBGRAPH and not a second `schemas` entry: overrides match on the entry's id, so reusing `schemas` would REPLACE this instance's schema graph rather than add to it -- the same trap the `cat-harness-src` entry above documents from the other side. REPOSITORY-scoped, like `bootstrap/skills/`: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency. This entry is the mirror of `folio-assistant-core/harness.json`'s own, and it has to be stated twice only because `resolveSkillDirs` has no caller -- when that is wired, THIS entry is the one to delete.

The `large-datasets` subgraph's instruction bodies. Declared here as well as in its own harness.json for the same reason kg-navigation is: `resolveSkillDirs` has no caller yet, so a nested instance's directories are not reachable from the root. `materialize-remote` lives here and is named by two diagrams in cat-harness/processes/ -- a skill ref resolves across the declared graphs, not within one directory. So no gate was failing. What WAS wrong is that the viewer already existed and nothing declared it: `docs-auto` renders one sub-page per skills directory, and `graph-tiles.undeclaredProjections` lists exactly a directory with a published page and no declared visualisation — so all seven read as "no published viewer" in the navbar tiles while being rendered the whole time. `tools` is the same `content` kind and has declared one all along, which is the precedent: declaring a visualiser for a content kind is a courtesy the corpus already extends, not an obligation this invents.

The who-iris instance's skills. ONE today -- `iris-dspace`, how IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core, and what a later tool needs from a record stated as checkable requirements. Deliberately thin, per the owner's 'mionimal tools in who specific stuff': the Dublin Core TYPE is generic and lives in folio-assist-core, the enumeration/subsetting descriptor lives in large-datasets, and OCR stays a cat-harness platform tool. What is WHO-specific is only how IRIS uses those things. So no gate was failing. The `large-datasets` subgraph's schema nodes -- `source-descriptor` (how to enumerate a corpus and ask it for a subset) and `artifact-store` (where an artifact too large for the site tree goes, as a declaration rather than a hardcoded host). Repository-scoped, so the path resolves against the REPO ROOT and carries no `../` -- a `../` prefix resolved OUTSIDE the checkout and every consumer silently dropped the entry (caught by CI, 2026-09-20).

The Zod that bootstrap's two published JSON Schemas are GENERATED from. Declared here AND in bootstrap-tools/harness.json, for the reason the sibling detangle/kg-navigation/large-datasets entries give: a directory declared only in an instance that is not a DEPENDENCY of this one is invisible from this root, because resolution walks this declaration plus its dependencies and bootstrap-tools is composed under the repository rather than depended on. Without this entry the schema graph reads 113 modules across four instances and bootstrap-tools contributes nothing — which is exactly the state this instance was created to end, since bootstrap itself contributed 0 of 113. The duplicate goes when the composition is wired, with the others.

directories._visualiser_comment: The docs-auto GLOSSARY INDEX, not `docs/glossary/index.html`. That was the declared value until 2026-09-22 and it was CIRCULAR: `docs/glossary/index.html` IS the state-visualiser's own page for this graph, so the page rendered “This graph is rendered elsewhere … the declaration names a visualiser for it: /glossary/” — pointing at the page you were reading. It was declared to make `published-graphs.md` count the graph as published, which made the count look right and the page say something false. The docs-auto index is a real rendering: 44 terms, each with the definition joined from the role registry.
directories.description: The swimlane glossary's retirement ledger. Declared rather than hidden because a consumer must be able to find what this instance has ever called a term: the glossary document is regenerated from the corpus each run and has no memory, so the one fact that cannot be re-derived — that a concept was once minted — is committed here. Keyed by the IRI's local part, never the absolute IRI, because the publication base is a deploy-time variable and a stored absolute IRI would rot the day it moved.

The platform's executable surface -- generators, checkers and the gate runner. THE LARGEST UNDECLARED DIRECTORY IN THE REPOSITORY until 2026-09-22 (bean `ylj7`): it holds more code than every declared directory here put together, and nothing declared it, so every consumer fanning out over declared directories skipped it and reported a clean run. Declared where it is rather than moved: these are ENTRY POINTS, named by path in `package.json` and in the CI workflows, which `check:ci-invocations` and `check:command-paths` exist to guard -- so a relocation is a large invocation surface for nothing the declaration does not already buy.

The MCP server and the harness runtime -- what `bun run cat-harness/src/index.ts` starts. `src/` is the name a new instance should use for its code by convention; it is a minority of the code HERE, which is the measurement that stopped `<stub>/src` from being adopted as a destination for everything.

The content-type adapters -- `DocumentContentAdapter` and the `PaperContentAdapter` that extends it. Code rather than schema: they are the behaviour the profiles select between, and `content-profiles` is the skill that says which axis they sit on.

The platform's own tests, EXCLUDING the results they write -- `test/results/` is declared `qa` and `test/health/results/` is declared `health`, and they keep those kinds. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of a graph, which is exactly this case: the tests are authored code, their outputs are state, and the two are told apart by what the files declare themselves to be.

_needs_comment: The layer this instance sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first.
_cat_bootstrap_comment: NO `bootstrap` DIRECTORY IS DECLARED HERE, and that is the owner's ruling of 2026-09-21 ("neither") on bean `pve3`, not an omission. This file used to declare `bootstrap/skills/` with `scope: "repository"`, which resolves against the REPOSITORY root rather than this instance — so bootstrap's skills and roles landed in folio-assistant's graph while the entry lived here. It did NOT declare `bootstrap/workflows/`, deliberately, because #432 measured bootstrap's process leaking into the root graph 88 times. The root therefore carried HALF of bootstrap, and the two symptoms were one asymmetry: a `lanes` entry on a bootstrap role minted `bindsLane -> role/<Lane>` pointing at a lane node only bootstrap's own export mints (four dangling links, measured 2026-09-21 by restoring `lanes` and watching `kg-export.test.ts` refuse it), and bootstrap's `kg-navigation` collided by name with `skills/folio-core/kg-navigation` in the published docs (bean `v3se`). `pve3` put the choice as BOTH halves or NEITHER; both would undo #432's isolation and put a process the root does not own into its published graph. Under NEITHER, bootstrap's skills are published through `bootstrap.jsonld` and its own instance page, which is where an instance's own graph belongs. The old entry's rationale is preserved in the bean rather than here, because a rationale for a declaration that no longer exists reads as a declaration to a skimming reader.
_associatedHarnesses_comment: Issue #1146. Owner, 2026-09-23: "i dont want to publish at /folio-assistant/ihris/; that's a platform change, certainly not a materialized publish, but we need a good mechanism for \"assocaiated\" harnesssed KGs." An associated harness is REFERENCED, never loaded: it is not in `needs`, nothing here builds or copies it, and it is published from its own repository at its own site. The Harnesses panel lists it under "Associated ↗ remote" and its ✎ goes to its own repository. Skill: associate-harness.
